We had a professional wrestler cutting off his thumb . We had a wannabe quitter scheming to try and be medically evacuated . We had a dude planting a fake idol and then accidentally finding his own fake idol. We had a woman losing her pants , a theater kid repeatedly making vampire analogies. I could go on and on about all the vibrant personalities, but with only two episodes to go in the season, it’s now becoming clear Survivor 51 might be best remembered for something else: producing one of the most dominant winners ever.

There are seven castaways left on Survivor 51 , and Sharonda is both the best connected player and the one who seems to be running the entire game. Fans have been all over her as the likely winner of the season for weeks, but this past episode in particular screamed her credentials from a helicopter in Fiji. She was given credit in very specific detail for engineering both of the last two votes, and as viewers, we’ve been told exactly where she stands with all the key players left in the game. I mean seriously, let’s just run down her relationships that have been spelled out explicitly.

She’s in a secret pact with Jelly and Devin as part of the helicopter alliance. As an audience, we have been told about this secret group since the first episode, but the remaining players still have no idea what’s going on. That alliance is clearly the main story of the season, and she is right at the center of it.

Then there’s Cristian, who we have seen Sharonda repeatedly manipulate. First he told her about Carter’s idol, then she lied and convinced him to turn on Maggie. It was only at the end of this past episode, after he watched Carter walk out the door, that he finally realized she’s not his friend. Then there’s Eric, who she straight up said she can get to do whatever she wants. I have to assume he feels the same way since he got no confessionals this week to rebut that.

We saw some tension between her and Mike this week, as she advocated for Carter being eliminated and he advocated for Thien An being eliminated. I bet you can guess who won that big showdown. Carter went home, and Mike ultimately voted with Sharonda, despite the fact that he had a final two alliance with the loveable farmer. Maybe he’ll give us a confessional next week where he explains why he went down that path, but from the perspective of the audience, it looks like she just barrelled over him and got her way.

Wait, How Many People Left Can Actually Win Survivor 51? Fans Aren’t Sure If A Survivor 51 Castaway Is Getting A Winner’s Edit Or Being Set Up For Heartbreak I Can’t Figure Out Which Survivor 51 Player Jeff Probst Was Talking About During A Pregame Interview Ordinarily, when Survivor shows us a player looking this dominant this early in the game, it’s a bad sign. It means everyone else is about to conspire to get them out because they’re such an obvious threat to win the game that they have to be eliminated. Maybe that’s what we’ll see with Sharonda, but I’m not so sure that’s going to happen this season. We’re not getting confessionals from other players about how she needs to be taken out, and there aren’t actually many people left in the game who the edit is telling us can win.

Seriously, who else can win this game right now? Jelly is definitely the other most likely contender. She’s gotten a main character edit, and we’ve heard castaways talk about how she’s a threat to win the game, but she got two total confessionals this past episode and players have repeatedly talked about getting her out during their confessionals. Devin still has an outside shot I guess. He’s this season’s leader in confessionals, but the edit has also repeatedly dunked on him for all the mistakes he has made.

I’m not saying Sharonda is for sure going to win Survivor 51 , but if she does win Survivor 51 , she is probably going to be remembered as one of the most dominant winners ever. She hasn’t had a single vote cast against her, and she’s voted correctly in every single tribal council so far, except the one where Linnea went home and multiple advantages were played . I’m not counting the Devin and Jelly vote because she’s the one who told them to play the idol and then told us, as an audience, very explicitly that she only voted against them so the rest of the tribe wouldn’t know she engineered the entire thing.

That's actually a positive for her, as is the fact that she’s formed the best relationships with the largest group of players. She also won an individual immunity idol and has gotten basically zero negative content from the edit. Seriously, what are her bad moments? I'll wait...

If Sharonda wins, it is going to look dominant, and we’re going to be talking about her in the same way we do Tony, Kim and other legends who gave us a masterclass. There’s still a long way to go, but at this point, I think it’s better than 50-50 it happens.

French actor Gérard Depardieu will face a criminal rape trial after an appeal from his lawyers failed.

According to Reuters , on Thursday the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that a trial would go ahead in relation to rape charges related to accusations from actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. She alleged that in August of that year, Depardieu had raped her twice at his Paris home. He was indicted in December 2020 and has denied any wrongdoing. articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF SUMMIT/LIONSGATE A joke from the original Twilight movie has been making the rounds ever since Robert Pattinson got cast as James Bond, and now the director has revealed that it was inspired by the way Pattinson looked on that day. In the scene, the character of Eric (Justin Chon) is announcing that the theme of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A joke from the original Twilight movie has been making the rounds ever since Robert Pattinson got cast as James Bond, and now the director has revealed that it was inspired by the way Pattinson looked on that day. In the scene, the character of Eric (Justin Chon) is announcing that the theme of the high school prom will be Monte Carlo, and one of the key elements will be "Bond. James Bond." The camera POV then moves to Pattinson's Edward, arriving to school in sunglasses with Kristen Stewart's Bella. On The Kyle Buchanan Show (as transcribed by Variety ), Twilight director Catherine Hardwicke revealed that the line was inspired by the way Pattinson looked in shades on set.

"That’s the one scene where I was like, ‘Let’s put the sunglasses on,'” she said. “He got out of the car and he looked so suave that he inspired the line, ‘Bond, James Bond.’ It was cool. We did think he looked like James Bond. I guess we were seeing the future." Four years later, in 2012, Pattinson said he would like to go for the role of Bond , but only when he hit the right age, saying, "It would be ridiculous to reinvent it as some young posh kid." ( Artemis Fowl tried the posh young kid approach, and proved Pattinson right.)

As the brooding, lonely vampire Edward Cullen, who falls for mortal Bella Swan but can't get intimate with her unless he turns her into a vampire too, Pattinson proved he could make masses of female fans swoon over him. Despite the competition from Taylor Lautner's abs, most of the self-professed Twi-hards were ultimately Team Edward. While The Twilight Saga proved a hit franchise on the strength of its female fan base, though, it was derided by critics and fans of more male-skewing franchises for its dedication to romance over world-building, and seemingly illogical changes to vampire mythology that had them sparkle in sunlight, and gave each one a different, X-Men like super power in addition to the immortality and blood-sucking.

Stewart had already proven her chops as a child actor, and immediately moved into more independent and artsy projects. Pattinson, on the other hand, had an uphill climb to prove to male fans that he wasn't just Edward Cullen. Working with directors like David Cronenberg and Christopher Nolan, he showed range and toughness, so that by the time he was cast as Batman, fans were only mildly skeptical, as opposed to when Michael Keaton and Ben Affleck got full-on hate. Once the movie was well-received, there was no question — if you can play Bruce Wayne, you can play James Bond. These days, it's Twilight that's being rebooted with a younger cast, and they can take on the roles without fear that they'll be typecast forever, knowing how their predecessors transcended it. (Taylor Lautner's abs are not available for comment.) Check out the full Catherine Hardwicke podcast below:

Would you have predicted Edward Cullen would become James Bond? You've got a license to comment your thoughts below.

"From trusted national figure to registered sex offender," says a voiceover in a new documentary for Channel 4 , Huw Edwards - Guilty .

The disgraced former BBC anchor is speaking publicly for the first time since the scandal that rocked Britain, letting cameras into his home over the course of a year. The film follows Edwards as he navigates his existence in the wake of grooming allegations and his 2024 conviction for making indecent images of children.

The journalist becomes the subject in a teaser released by Channel 4 on Thursday, as Edwards becomes visibly fraught while questioned. "You want me to analyze what I was doing? I mean, seriously?" Edwards asks. The ex-newscaster, who hosted the BBC’s flagship News at Ten program and led landmark coverage for the corporation — including the death of Queen Elizabeth II and the London 2012 Olympics — was arrested in November 2023 and charged the following July after he was found to have 41 indecent images of children sent to him by another man, a convicted pedophile, on WhatsApp. Seven of the photos were category A images, the most severe classification, two of which showed a child between seven and nine. He was handed a six-month sentence, suspended for two years.

Following several attempts to ingratiate himself back into public life, Channel 4 says Edwards is forced to confront his loss of fame, declining health, fractured relationships, and his crimes in the documentary.

articles.title: NBC Is Airing Last Year’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, But Social Media Users Have A Way Better Idea
articles.summary: No parade? No problem.
articles.content:
I’ve got to be honest. I was NOT dreaming of a white Thanksgiving this week, but that’s what people in many parts of the country got. If you got up this morning wondering how to watch the 100th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade , you may have gotten a rude awakening: It’s not hitting the 2026 TV schedule until Saturday. NBC does have a Turkey Day solution, but honestly, it’s not the one people on the Internet want.

On Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. NBC may have 99 problems, but no parade ain’t one. It’s not a bad idea really. The big balloons, c-list singers, and jazzy dance breaks are usually something most of us have on in the background anyway on this auspicious day. But social media users have a way better idea.

They later joked the lineup from 2003 “looked pretty good.” Another user had a specific year request, too, writing :

This isn't the first Macy's Day Parade controversy this season. If you'd rather go the nostalgia play, another X user even noted you can throw one of these old episodes on via YouTube, and I thank this individual for that hot tip.

It seems as if NBC’s strategy is the network doesn't want viewers to notice the parade is old, but there will be moments anyone actually paying attention to the broadcast should notice. I’m not saying that’s the world’s worst strategy given I already established a lot of us watch this while doing other tasks. Still, I think just going full in and putting on an older broadcast would be really fun, and I think would inspire people to pay closer attention and see what cultural references from the time are mentioned and what’s changed in the decades since.

And if the movie’s anything like Avengers: Infinity War , then it will end on a massive cliffhanger with the Ruler of Latveria emerging victorious and leading us directly to Avengers: Secret Wars . Of all of Marvel Comics ’ villains, Doctor Doom arguably has the best track record when it comes to defeating his heroic enemies. With his mastery of science and magic, along with his tactical mind, Doom views his triumph as inevitable and some of them actually are. Even Marvel’s greatest heroes sometimes kneel before Doom's might.

These are the events where Doctor Doom undoubtedly came out on top. And even if his storylines eventually have him lose his position, the fact that he had those triumphs in the first place makes him unlike any other villain in the Marvel Universe.

One of the defining moments in Doctor Doom’s life was when he scarred his face during a college experiment. Doom wanted to create a device that would let him go to Hell and save the soul of his mother, Cynthia, from the demon Mephisto. This mission has been central to Doom’s motivations for decades. Eventually, Doom becomes so desperate that he does the unthinkable and reaches out to someone else for help. Working with Doctor Strange, the two master sorcerers battled their way through Mephisto’s demon army. However, Doom seemed to double-cross Strange by offering Strange’s soul to Mephisto in exchange for Cynthia’s, a bargain which she vehemently objected to. Yet Doom’s betrayal was all a trick, as he helped Strange escape Mephisto as well. Freed from her contract with Mephisto, Cynthia was finally allowed to find peace in Heaven. Doctor Doom might be an egomaniacal dictator, but he’ll do anything for his mother.

A huge part of Doctor Doom’s identity is that he is the ruler of the small nation of Latveria. One of the best stories that explains exactly how Doom conquered his homeland is the prequel miniseries Books of Doom , which chronicles the villain’s rise to power. After suffering a horrific childhood with his parents dying at the hands of Latveria’s corrupt elite, Doom left his home to travel the world. By the time he returned years later, he had become the armored master of sorcery and science that we all know today. With his vast power and his promise to liberate the people of Latveria from King Vladimir's tyranny, Doom inspired a revolution. Ultimately, Doom avenged his parents’ murderer by strangling Vladimir with his bare hands. As Latveria’s new ruler, Doom turned the third-world country into one of the most powerful and prosperous nations on Earth with free healthcare and education for all its citizens. Doom is a villain who truly believes he can make the world a better place, and Latveria is the best evidence of his success.

Doctor Doom is always trying to take over the world, but when he was appointed the new Sorcerer Supreme, he finally had the power to do so. Within a single day, all world leaders surrendered to Doom’s will. All nations became part of a United Latveria, and Doom allowed the world governments to remain as long as they answered to him. During his reign, Doom ended all wars, created universal health care and education, and even turned Hydra into a force for good. However, as with Doctor Doom, darkness lurked beneath this seeming utopia. Several heroes snuck into Latveria and discovered the awful truth. Doom had detained every citizen of Latveria and was draining their life forces. Once the truth was revealed, Doom’s empire came crumbling down. Ultimately, Doom would sacrifice his life to resurrect his goddaughter Valeria, who was killed during the conflict. Although his reign came to an end, Doom was Earth’s sole ruler for a time.

Taking over Earth is one thing, but Doctor Doom’s death led him to an even greater achievement: conquering Hell itself. After the events of One World Under Doom , the former ruler of Latveria and Earth was sent to Hell for his countless crimes. The “Hell’s Angel” storyline has Doom temporarily bring a comatose Captain America to Hell so they could raise a rebellion to overthrow Mephisto and free countless demons and human sinners. Doom and Captain America fought side by side against Mephisto’s loyal soldiers while inspiring rebellion wherever they went. However, during the final battle, Doom seemed to betray Captain America and let Mephisto consume the First Avenger's soul. But it was yet another trick against Mephisto. Doom had placed shards of the all-powerful weapon called the Antidivine in Captain America’s soul. When Mephisto tried to consume it, he instantly became frail and was then beaten by Doom. Thereupon, Doom forced Mephisto to make him the new King of Hell.

When the entire Marvel Multiverse was falling apart because of the Beyonders and Incursions, it wasn’t the Avengers, X-Men, or Fantastic Four who saved the day; it was Doom. As the last worlds were destroyed, Doctor Doom worked with Doctor Strange and Molecule Man to kill the omnipotent Beyonders and steal their powers. With this newfound power, God Emperor Doom gathered the last remnants of various universes and created the patchwork planet Battleworld. From his throne, Doom saved all he could, and most of Battleworld’s population looked to him as their lord and savior. The 2015 Secret Wars event also saw Doom achieve other great victories, defeating Phoenix Cyclops, Thanos, Doctor Strange, and even an Infinity Gauntlet-wielding Black Panther. Of course, Doom’s own insecurities would lead to his loss of godhood at the hands of Mr. Fantastic. Still, Doom conquered some of the multiverse's most powerful beings and saved billions of lives from multiversal collapse.

What’s your favorite Doctor Doom victory? Leave a comment below and join the conversation in the  ComicBook Forum!

Gérard Depardieu will stand trial in a criminal court on a rape charge related to accusations by actress Charlotte Arnould, after an appeal by his lawyers failed.

The Paris Court of Appeal said on Thursday that Depardieu would be tried for one part of the accusations levelled by Arnould against the actor.

The actress, whose father was an old friend of the actor, accuses Depardieu of raping and sexually assaulting her twice in his Paris mansion in the summer of 2018 after she went to him for acting advice. articles.title: Borderlands 4 Is Cheaper Than Ever Before for Black Friday
articles.summary: Borderlands 4 is seeing a huge discount, marked down a massive 79%, which brings its price to just $15. This deal comes in time for Black Friday and makes it one of the best opportunities to jump into the series' latest entry. With how expensive AAA gaming has become, sales like these can save players' […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Borderlands 4 is seeing a huge discount, marked down a massive 79%, which brings its price to just $15. This deal comes in time for Black Friday and makes it one of the best opportunities to jump into the series' latest entry. With how expensive AAA gaming has become, sales like these can save players' wallets. The industry often sees many of the most popular games go on sale for Black Friday and the holidays, but discounts of this magnitude are not generally seen. There is no telling how long Borderlands 4's sale will go on or if it will sell out, so fans should act quickly.

The deal can be found on Amazon and other retailers, where the physical version of Borderlands 4 on PlayStation 5 is marked down to $15.00 , making it the lowest price the game has seen since its release in 2025 . There may never be another sale this low. The latest entry in the popular looter shooter series offers another opportunity to hunt down legendary weapons, experiment with character builds, and cause chaos alongside friends. It is worth it at full price, but this sale makes purchasing it a no-brainer for anyone on the fence.

Discounts vary depending on your platform and whether you prefer physical or digital games, with PS5 offering the best deal at $15.00. That said, Xbox Series X players can get their hands on a physical copy between $15.00 and $19.99. Sadly, PC players are not as lucky as a code for Borderlands 4 still runs $49.99. Sadly, there is no option for Nintendo Switch players . These deals are available on Amazon , Best Buy , Target , and GameStop .

There is no stated period for the sale, so it could very well end after Black Friday. Physical editions could also see limited stock and may sell out before you can purchase a copy. Digital versions do not have this worry, but the physical versions offer the best sale currently.

For those unfamiliar with Borderlands 4 , Gearbox takes players away from Pandora and introduces them to Kairos, a planet ruled by the Timekeeper. Players can choose from four new Vault Hunters, each featuring distinct abilities and skill trees. It has enhanced the exploration aspect with new abilities and mechanics, making traversal and combat more dynamic.

One of the biggest draws of the Borderlands series has always been its cooperative multiplayer, and that is true here. Borderlands 4 supports up to four players in online co-op, with individual difficulty settings and level scaling to accommodate different skill levels. That said, it can also be enjoyed solo, even if multiplayer is a more full experience. Players can expect between 30 and 100 hours of chaotic shooting fun in Borderlands 4 , and now for the low price of $15.

articles.title: How 'The Lowdown' Season 2 Finale Sets Up a (Hoped for) Third Season
articles.summary: Creator Sterlin Harjo and Ethan Hawke break down Lee's growth as a person and the loose threads still left to explore.
articles.content:
[This story contains spoilers for season two of The Lowdown and "The Tower," the Nov. 25 season finale.]

The first season of The Lowdown had a pretty clear resolution : The story that "truthstorian" Lee Raybon ( Ethan Hawke ) had been chasing throughout the season — about the death of the brother (Tim Blake Nelson) of Oklahoma's likely next governor (Kyle Maclachlan) and their family's corrupt history — was printed (if not in the form he initially thought) and seemingly put to rest.

Season two, however, concludes with multiple threads still untied — and some even circling back to season one. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'American Horror Story' Finale: Paul Anthony Kelly on the Season 13 Ending: "I Was Flabbergasted" TV 'Snowfall' Spinoff Boss Malcolm Spellman Lays Out Multi-Season Plan for 'The Drop,' Why Season One Was Just a "Dash of What's Coming"

Lee, with help from some of the journalists he disparaged at the beginning of the season, gets an exposé on conditions at Judge Sallsman's (John Hawkes) Fresh Start meatpacking operations published, but he's frustrated that he can't tie the judge himself to the story. As he continues chasing leads — including getting Martha Plimpton's Sheriff Thorne to go on record about the judge — Marty (Keith David) saves Lee from walking into a confrontation with some of the people behind last season's One Well conspiracy. They realize that Lee's story about Fresh Start, the One Well people and Marty's investigation of the illicit sale of indigenous artifacts are all part of a bigger picture. Ginger (Betty Gilpin), meanwhile, leaves Tulsa after realizing that, for several reasons, she can't continue her life there.

In other words, there is a lot left to explore in a potential third season — which FX hasn't decided on yet.

"I'm trying to twist their arm," The Lowdown creator and showrunner Sterlin Harjo told The Hollywood Reporter about the very open-ended finale. "We left it open and pushed forward to a season three because I like three-season shows. I don't know if we're going to be doing it, but I hope that we are." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The finale, titled "The Tower," did offer closure on one front: Lee, his daughter Francis (Ryan Kiera Armstrong) and their family and friends lay Tommy Lee Jones' Lee Sr., aka Frog, to rest at a somewhat chaotic funeral, which features the return of Peter Dinklage as Lee's friend Wendell, who eulogizes Frog with a reading of Dylan Thomas' "Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night." That's followed by a more relaxed, and touching, gathering at Sweet Emily's afterward, where Francis reads a journal entry of Frog's detailing the apprehension he felt about being a father when Lee was a baby.

"He's going through the stages of grief. How he understands and reinterprets he and his father's relationship now that his father's gone, it's going to be an ever-changing thing," Hawke tells THR . "But I feel like something positive and profound happens to Lee when his daughter is reading to him."

Harjo and Hawke talked with THR about the loose plot threads, Lee's ongoing work of becoming a better person, and how a conversation between Harjo and Jones led to the finale's prologue. (Separate interviews are combined and edited below.)

Before we talk about the end of the season, I want to go back to episode six — where Frog dies at the end of a father-son road trip — because the scenes with Ethan and Tommy are just so, so good. It seems like a huge theme of the season of Lee coming to terms with his dad. He's kind of starting to get there throughout that episode, but there's still a lot left for him to process. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

STERLIN HARJO I would say so. You have this like these two guys that don't communicate well. I kind of like compare it to the Tim and Dawn love story in the English Office . They have to hide all of their affection, so a touch on the shoulder becomes like a kiss. It's similar with Lee and Frog because they don't communicate. These small gestures end up feeling really big. I think them connecting and going home, they don't say 'I love you' or anything like that. But he touches his son on the back. He tells some stories about [Lee's] mother. All of these things are really big, because they don't communicate that well, and they have a hard time meeting each other in the middle.

I think that that last scene is beautiful where Frog says to Lee, you know, and it almost escapes out of his mouth, "It wasn't so bad in there, the hospital, and I might have needed a rest." That's the apology. Lee is kind of shocked and can't say anything, and he just nods, which is also his apology and acknowledgement of it. It's really beautiful moment. And those are my kids that are playing with the bubbles [as Frog watches Lee walk into the convenience store]. I'm really proud of all that.

ETHAN HAWKE What I like about the writing of the show is it's never one thing. It's like more like real life. There is the possibility of healing. It kind of dawns on him at the end of episode six that his father wants to make up with him. And if his father wants to do that, then his father is a different man than he had assumed he was. That opportunity for healing existing is a great benefit to Lee. But of course, they don't really get to resolve it, and that's the beauty of episode eight when his daughter is reading from [Frog's] journal to him. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Would the Lee of season one have been able to hand off the Fresh Start story?

HAWKE No. Those are the small growths that you get to show in a TV show. What I love about it, having never made a TV show before, the canvas size is just so big that you can really get intimate with a character and show those little adjustments. I don't think at the beginning of season one that he would have been able to go to his ex-wife's wedding and not make it about himself. That was a small journey. This journey of showing respect to other journalists was [another].

HARJO It's such a big deal for me. I wanted that to be a big moment. I opened the season with him calling everyone sellouts and assholes, and then he has to humble himself and go to all of them, hat in hand, and say I need your help. I think it's also a part of the growth of his personal life and the relationship with his father — him having to realize that he's not the only one. The story isn't just about him.

There are a lot more loose ends at the end of this season than there were at the end of season one.

HARJO We've got to twist FX and Disney's arm for season three. I don't know how the powers that be work that out. It sure would help if we had awards. Somehow, the Hollywood awards have always been elusive to me and my projects, even though they get reviewed so well. We'll see what happens, but hopefully something like that happens and that helps us a little bit. I don't know where we stand right now. I hope to do a season three. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Assuming you do go get to go forward — I hope so too — would those loose ends be the primary plot driver in a third season, or more secondary?

HARJO It will be the plot of season three, that bigger conspiracy. Obviously there will be some surprises, but what I wanted to do was the idea that season one, you feel like it's one and done. This is the conspiracy. Then we're moving on to another conspiracy in season two. One of the things I keep saying in season one is everything's connected. And actually in Reservation Dogs , we said that a lot too. But the idea is that we were kind of pretending it was going to be these two separate things, but actually they're all connected.

HAWKE The setup is pretty clear. At the end of season two, we see that there's a connection between the crime of season one and the crime of season two. There's a connection between this judge and One Well. I think season three would be about bringing the whole tower down.

From a character perspective, what do you want to keep exploring with Lee?

HAWKE We've always kind of dreamed of this as a trilogy. Put simply, season one is about him learning how to be a father, and season two is learning about how to be a son, and a third season would be about him learning to live with himself, and completing the hero's journey.

HARJO I'm really interested in season three being about, What is it like watching your daughter become the next stage of all of that? And also, what does it mean to slow down? What does it mean to look at your life and go, OK, I don't always have to chase the truth at the detriment of my health, I can also have balance. How do I balance my life, find happiness and find love, and I'm able to be a father and a son and also someone that fights for the truth. How do we become a whole human being and be more responsible? I think that is in the cards for Lee. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

There weren't any obvious markers for where Ginger has ended up in her final scene. Where is she as she tries to get away from her former life?

HARJO She's in Eureka Springs [Arkansas], which is a couple hours away from Tulsa going east, and it's just an interesting old mining and brothel town. It's really beautiful, in the Ozarks, and a great place to go to get away. We broke off with Betty and took a small group to Eureka Springs and filmed that.

I also wanted to ask about the prologue scene in the finale, showing Frog at the fireworks stand in Texas and watching Paris, Texas , which the opening scene of the season pays homage to. Did you just want to give people a sense of where he started this season?

HARJO Tommy Lee Jones would call me up now and again. "Hey, I want to talk about the script. You want to come over?" I'd go to his house, and his wife Dawn was awesome, and we would talk about polo or whatever for a little bit. Then he'd say, "All right, come back here," and we'd go into his office and start talking about the script. At one point, he goes, "Would you like to know where Frog came from?" And I was like, "What do you mean?" He's like, "Well, the backstory that I came up with." I was like, "Yeah, of course." He just told me that story, and I was amazed. It was just the backstory that he had invented — Frog was in Palestine, Texas, working at this fireworks stand. He told me this story, and I was like, "Well, I've got to do that. I have to put that in the finale." So we did.

This first Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake doesn't do much.

The new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake update is specifically the 1.1.2 update. And while it doesn't do much, Nintendo has provided the patch notes for it, which consist of two lines. One of these notes the new Zelda update fixes "several issues" that will provide a smother smoother gameplay experience. How many fixed issues are contained within this, we don't know. Could be a few, dozens, or even hundreds. Unfortunately, Nintendo patch notes aren't the most transparent, and these are no exception.

There is one fix it felt the need to highlight, though, which is the other line of the patch notes. This line reveals Nintendo has fixed the event where "Malon's Event" could not be progressed. This being highlighted suggests every other fix lumped together in the other line is less significant than this one; otherwise, it would be highlighted as well. This doesn't narrow the field much, though, because this is a pretty substantial fix.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is available via the Nintendo Switch 2, and the Nintendo Switch 2 only.

articles.title: Happy Thanksgiving, Netflix Just Canceled Two Shows With Major Stars
articles.summary: The streaming service is at it again.
articles.content:
Thanksgiving is officially upon us, and many TV and movie fans are going to be re-watching their favorite festive programming. Whether its Friends ' Thanksgiving episodes or a trip to Star's Hallow from Gilmore Girls , there's plenty to chose from. Unfortunately we got some bad news for TV addicts, specifically those with a Netflix subscription . Namely that the streaming platform has cancelled two more shows after just one season , and they both star big celebrities.

Then there's Amsterdam Empire , which had arguably less hype around it than Ferrell's comedy series. Starring Famke Janssen ( Goldeneye , The X-Men movies ), the show followed her character Betty Jonkers, a former pop star whose coffee-mogul husband is hiding some shady dealings. The show was shot entirely in Dutch, which is the accomplished actress' first language. Unfortunately the show is now over after just one season, which ended on an exciting cliffhanger. This comes after Janssen was noticeably left out of Avengers: Doomsday , despite so many of her X-Men co-stars reprising their roles in the upcoming Marvel movie .

These two titles join the ranks of many shows that Netflix has dropped way too early, to dismay of fans. Some other titles to have suffered this fate include The OA , which was cancelled after two wild seasons and a huge cliffhanger. Then there was Sense8 , which got cancelled but eventually got a movie finale after fans made their voices known. Fans have also been hoping to see more of David Fincher's Mindhunter since the last episode aired back in 2019.

articles.title: Star Trek's Thanksgiving Episode Is The Ultimate Holiday Get-Together Gone Wrong
articles.summary: As families gather around the dinner table for the winter holidays, there's one feeling that invades their bodies more than upset stomachs from undercooked turkey. It's the dread and anxiety that come with being forced around family members who you would otherwise never volunteer to see, let alone joining them to eat a meal. Most […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As families gather around the dinner table for the winter holidays, there's one feeling that invades their bodies more than upset stomachs from undercooked turkey. It's the dread and anxiety that come with being forced around family members who you would otherwise never volunteer to see, let alone joining them to eat a meal. Most Thanksgiving TV specials focus on gratitude and finding a middle ground to get along with relatives, but there is a reason those shows are fiction and not real-life. There's one episode of a classic sci-fi show that happens to take place on Thanksgiving, and its table-side etiquette will remind you that things could always be worse, especially if your guest has unlimited cosmic powers at their beckon.

"Charlie X" from Star Trek's debut season is a great example of a sci-fi trope that continues to be played out in the genre to this very day. It centers on an overpowered being with little grasp on humanity and how to be responsible with their abilities, resulting in some very uncomfortable situations for Captain Kirk's crew. The storyline is only a Thanksgiving episode due to its apparent stardate and a handful of throwaway lines of dialogue, but it actually has a hidden holiday message that you might want to take to the heart to your next family gathering. Or, you can learn a piece of obscure Star Trek trivia that very few people are aware of and use that to escape a conversation with your very politically-charged aunt or uncle . The choice is yours, which is more than we can say for poor Charlie.

"Charlie X" was part of the first draft proposal Roddenberry used to shop the series around in 1964. Under the working title of "The Day Charlie Became God," its synopsis read as "the accidental occurrence of infinite power to do all things, in the hands of a very finite man." No mention was made of how old this mortal being was, but making them into a moody teenager was a genius play that was a perfect fit for this script. When the finalized version aired on Sep. 15, 1966, the series had only just started and NBC viewers were still getting used to the idea of creator Gene Roddenberry's vision for " Wagon Train to the stars." What they weren't prepared for was intergalactic teenage melodrama along with their sci-fi that made for an hour of unexpectedly good television.

Strange things start happening on board the USS Enterprise after picking up Charlie Evans, a socially awkward teen who spent nearly all of his life alone on an uninhabited planet. Not only are they weird in the sense of odd coincidences happening whenever Charlie is around such as playing cards changing face or Thanksgiving meals appearing out of thin air (more on that later), but dangerous such as starships exploding to smithereens or crew members mysteriously disappearing when he is angered. It doesn't take long for Kirk, Spock and McCoy to suss out what is happening, and deduce that their adolescent passenger may be a Thasian, a race of extremely powerful beings in the same vein as Trelane or a member of the Q Continuum . However, those aliens are non-corporeal, and Dr. McCoy's scans prove Charlie is a human. The problem then becomes how do you discipline a spiteful teen boy with raging hormones who can snap his finger and make everyone disappear?

After Charlie's secret is exposed, he stops trying to hide his desires and commandeers the starship with his powers to fast travel to Colony Alpha V, the last known home of any of his relatives. His list of victims rapidly grows, as he turns one girl he liked into an iguana while another female crew member has her face completely removed. Kirk knows Charlie can destroy their entire vessel whenever he feels like it, so he and his advisors work quietly to find a way to stop him. As their plan takes shape and begins to work, an unexpected non-corporeal visitor arrives — a representative from Thasius who explains who Charlie is and how he was gifted his powers. Just as easily as Charlie was given his powers, so too can they take them, and the green entity beams a screaming Charlie away to be taught a lesson in respect and possibly worse.

This offbeat episode holds one unique distinction in Star Trek history as being the only episode of the series that Roddenberry performed in. While Roddenberry was credited as Producer and writer (even though D.C. Fontana developed the story and wrote the teleplay), he was also an actor in "Charlie X." His role as the galley chef seen towards the end of the first act is partially obscured by set decoration and hidden by him turning his back to the camera, leaving this Easter Egg as a special one for those hardcore Trekkies in the know. Roddenberry's fleeting Trek cameo is also the moment where we learn the date of when these events unfold. "On Earth today it's Thanksgiving," Captain Kirk explains to the cook. "If the crew has to eat synthetic meatloaf, I want it to look like Turkey." His voice can be heard later in the episode after Charlie destroys the Antares, explaining that real turkeys suddenly appeared baking in the oven, a surprise to Kirk that starts him questioning who his new passenger truly is. Oh, and those turkeys for the ship's Thanksgiving dinner were probably burnt to a crisp during Charlie's tantrum turned takeover, so their meal for the evening was likely more of those pastel-colored cubes that never seemed very appetizing to begin with.

Star Trek has featured many great feasts over the years, including the awkward dinner between Kirk's crew and the Klingons in Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country , and "Forget Me Not" from Discovery's third season. There's even still time for a Thanksgiving Celebration while war rages on in Deep Space Nine , as there's a mention of Captain Sisko's impressive homemade turkey dinner with all the trimmings during "Blaze of Glory" from its fifth season. But as far as rough Thanksgiving celebrations go, none could be as brutal as Charlie X's visit to the Enterprise. Unseasoned mashed potatoes and cold turkey are nothing in comparison to having your eyes, mouth and nose wiped away from your face. So remember when you are eating your pecan pie while watching the clock tick down so you can make your getaway from your relatives to avoid another intense discussion about American politics and "the problem with today's generation," be grateful that none of them have godlike powers that could warp you to the Gamma Quadrant without an EV suit. Now, please pass the sweet potatoes — I've got some TOS to binge.

What did you think of "Charlie X" as an episode? Is it a must-watch or an easy pass? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments.

articles.title: One Thing Stephen Colbert Neglected While He Was On Late Night His Wife Wants Him To Get Into
articles.summary: I totally see how this happened.
articles.content:
It’s hard to believe The Late Show with Stephen Colbert has been off of the air for half a year now. It’s presence was so undeniable for so long, sometimes I still feel like it’s around even though it’s definitely cancelled . Stephen Colbert ’s kept busy, of course. He’s writing an LOTR movie (though we’ll have to see how it pans out after that merger )! Now that he does have more downtime he’s said there’s something his wife wants him to get into.

The man was taking a slew of questions from his fellow late night hosts in a profile with THR when he admitted to wanting to get fit, fit, fit. The only time I’ve ever seen Stephen Colbert really attempt anything related to fitness was like eight years ago when The Late Show did an interview with the late Ruth Bader Ginsberg that included mobility stretches and some minor lifting, oh and one shot of Stephen Colbert pulling up his shirt and exposing his all-time dad bod.

I can hardly blame the former late night host for not making the time for exercise. We learned a few months ago his writing team was working long hours and making monologue changes on the fly in order to stay ahead of social media during their later filming days. The thanks they got was getting fired and having just a few days to exit the studio . His stuff was shipped off to a museum. He went to his brother’s wedding, and then moved on. The one upside is now he has all the time in the world to get into shape.

So far, we haven’t seen Stephen Colbert become a fitness influencer in the days since The Late Show ended. However, there’s always time, and I will certainly be keeping my eyes peeled the next time the former late night host makes an appearance. Is that arm definition? Is there any hint of abs? Only time will tell.

articles.title: I Never Knew How Miserable Star Trek's Worst Fight Was To Film, But William Shatner Laid It Out
articles.summary: I never guessed it was so bad.
articles.content:
One of Star Tre k's most iconic fight scenes was also one of the most miserable to film. William Shatner recently talked about how bad it was to do the Gorn fight in the original series, and how it felt even worse to actually shoot than it looked onscreen.

The "regolith," which by the way are the minerals that settle on top of bedrock, were so abrasive that it made the fight very difficult to film. I'm sure most Star Trek fans don't need to rewatch the scene with a Paramount+ subscription to know the end result ultimately wasn't worth the pain and toil. Still, lame fight aside, "Arena" is a pretty compelling episode.

"Arena" starts when Kirk and the Gorn are transported to the planet to battle thanks to a third species named the Metrons. The Metrons wish to see a fight to the death, but are impressed when Kirk outmaneuvers the Gorn and spares its life instead. Both are then returned to their ship, with the lesson being that brains can overcome brawn with some quick thinking and skills.

articles.title: Every MCU Character Who Knows About the Multiverse Ahead of Avengers: Doomsday (And What They Know)
articles.summary: The Multiverse is about to become very crowded when Avengers: Doomsday finally makes its long-anticipated theatrical debut this December. While most MCU fans are well aware of what these parallel dimensions are all about, not every superhero has been clued in yet. As helpful as it would be if every Avenger subscribed to Doctor Strange's […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Multiverse is about to become very crowded when Avengers: Doomsday finally makes its long-anticipated theatrical debut this December. While most MCU fans are well aware of what these parallel dimensions are all about, not every superhero has been clued in yet. As helpful as it would be if every Avenger subscribed to Doctor Strange's Substack to stay in the know about these sort of things, the majority of MCU heroes have only the faintest idea about time travel being a possibility, and an even greater number are completely oblivious to branching realities and stick to their worldly struggles instead of worrying about something bigger and more abstract beyond their universe.

Only a select few have been directly affected by the Multiverse, and most of them have never crossed paths with each other — or at least, not yet. Here's our list of superheroes who have experience in multi-dimensional affairs and might be highly useful in handling whatever malevolent plans Doctor Doom has in store for the MCU. Consider this your only warning - this article is filled with spoilers from the last ten years of every Marvel TV show and movie. If you've already binged everything then you have nothing to worry about, but if you're new to this, either walk away now or prepare to get a crash course in the Multiverse from about a dozen superheroes who have already dealt with this concept at least once and walked away from it still standing.

This is the easiest name to add to this list, because Doctor Strange might have very well been the first MCU superhero to first hear about this concept in his very first movie back in 2016. Strange's first steps towards learning about the multiverse was teased in that solo debut, and as his education in sorcery grew so too did his information about the infinite possibilities of every world beyond his own.

Strange has been responsible for informing several others on this list about the multiverse and how it may or may not directly affect their lives. His ability to traverse the different dimensions is what led him and his team of sorcerers led by Wong to find versions of Earth's mightiest heroes to help take down Thanos and his army in Endgame . What truly made his head spin was meeting the Illuminati in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , which led to his meeting of dimension-hopping America Chavez who is a specialist in moving around the multiverse. At the end of that movie, Strange had his first run-in with Clea (played by Charlize Theron) who informed the doctor that his actions caused an incursion and she requires his help to fix the multiversal damage.

The events of No Way Home opened the doors of the multiverse for Peter Parker, along with his friends Ned and MJ. His attempt at magic backfired in classic Parker fashion, opening up space for the Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire versions of Spidey to enter his timeline, along with a handful of their villains. The trio of web-heads were able to secure their respective bad guys and send them back to their dimensions of origins, while Ned learned he could handle a Sling Ring pretty well for someone with no background in sorcery.

The movie ends with Peter deciding the best way to protect the multiverse is to extinguish the memory of his existence from anyone who knew him, including his friends. With some hesitation, Strange obliges and casts the spell, leaving Parker completely alone as the only person who remembered anything he had accomplished in that universe. It's a mandate in both the comics and movies that "Peter Parker must suffer," but that didn't make that scene any less harsh to watch. This incident has yet to be reversed, and may very well stay as is, but the fact that Parker has some surprising knowledge about the multiverse is bound to be useful in Doomsday .

The former God of Mischief turned God of Stories might be the key to the Multiverse as events unfold. Despite his demise at Thanos' hands in Infinity War , Loki reentered the timeline thanks to the Infinity Stone heists seen in Endgame . However, his incursion alerted the TVA to his presence and quickly recruited the Asgardian magician into their fold. Through his employment with this organization, Loki became a walking encyclopedia on the Multiverse and is now the element that binds every branching reality together. He might be the most important player in this story , and would certainly be a target for Doom if he learned about Loki's new role.

Along with Loki, we can't neglect Sylvie, who was introduced in the Loki series and is another hero who understands the gravity of these multiple realities. She flip-flopped from chaotic neutral to evil and then back to good during the show's second season but ultimately realized her mistake and after being given a second chance by Loki has enjoyed her freedom from being no longer pursued by the TVA. Her participation in Doomsday has not been confirmed yet but there are rumors of her possibly making her cinematic debut as one of Doom's witches. However, this latest bit of info has people thinking the Green Witch might be someone else entirely .

Rambeau gained her powers in WandaVision , which was also the first time she understood that the Multiverse was an actual thing. It wasn't until The Marvels film from 2023 that she got her first real taste of it. While trying to fix a rupture between realities, Rambeau is trapped on the other side and awakens in a mid-credits scene in an unfamiliar medical facility. There, she sees who she thinks is her mom but is actually an alternate-reality version of Maria Rambeau, who is revealed to be Binary by the end of the shocking scene.

Making an even bigger impact was the MCU debut of Hank McCoy AKA The Beast , played once again by Kelsey Grammar. The furry blue mutant explains that he believes she crossed through a tear in time and space and ended up in this parallel dimension with them, adding him to this list of heroes in the know about multiversal exploits. Their ability to enter other worlds is an X-factor in this scenario, but their world seems different from the one that we've previously seen X-Men reside in. Photon has made some great allies by stumbling into the perfect dimension for her on sheer luck, so we will see how she and her new friends (and sort of mom but not really) enter the picture when it comes to Doctor Doom.

Banner's understanding of the multiverse may be hypothetical when he first learned about the possibilities of branching realities via the Ancient One in Avengers: Infinity War . After being easily defeated in his Hulk form, Banner inquires about taking the Ancient One's Time Stone, who shows him a visualization of the flow of time and how that affects every path beyond it. It wasn't exactly a lecture on the multiverse, but it did begin to show the potential for what lies beyond Earth-616.

In his scene from Endgame's encore presentation, Banner has locked himself in a subterranean facility to prevent himself or any others from reaching him after an unexpected "incident" involving the Hulk breaking free and going on a rampage for the first time in a decade. While the scientist investigates a Gamma-suppression system with promising results, he is interrupted by something else green and mean — the arrival of Doctor Doom. The familiar roar of the Hulk echoes in the building and moments later, both characters are gone as a verdant symbol on the floor glows. We don't know what Banner knows yet, but there is a strong chance he's in on the secret now thanks to Doom.

Scott Lang is acutely aware of the breadth of the multiverse, first learning about it while being lost in the Quantum Realm following Thanos' finger snap, as seen during a mid-credits scene in Ant-Man and The Wasp . His time adrift in this liminal space led to the Avengers using time-travel as a means to grabbing the Infinity Stones in Endgame , but it was what happened after that film which turned up the heat for the multiverse and where Janet van Dyne comes into play.

Kang the Conqueror was introduced in the Loki series on Disney+, but his presence was felt in a bigger way during Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania . Like all bad guys, Kang was defeated but not before Lang and van Dyne were made very aware of the existence of alternate worlds and multiple versions of Kang. While this major foe of the Avengers was put out of commission and ultimately replaced by Doom, he remains the catalyst to the multiverse opening up in the MCU and the reason that these two characters will be valuable resources in the coming clash.

When Wanda used her magic to create alternate realities around herself to protect her psyche following Vision's death in WandaVision , her final confrontation with Agatha Harkness led to an awakening within her powers. As she fully became the Scarlet Witch by embracing the power of the Darkhold, a different MCU TV show was happening simultaneously that acknowledged the moment we crossed the threshold. Loki and Sylvie were hanging out with Kang — the He Who Remains version of the Conqueror— when he realized something major had happened, and the multiverse would never be the same again.

Things picked up in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness as mentioned earlier, with Wanda believing she could reunite with her fictional children from WandaVision by traveling the Multiverse to seek versions of them out for herself. Instead, she's been causing cataclysmic events wherever she dreamwalks, forcing Strange, Wong, Chavez and Baron Mordo to battle and stop her incursions on the multiverse. She was last seen being recruited by Doom at the end of VisionQuest , discovering her body buried under rubble in Mount Wundagore and seemingly taking control of her mind and power for his own evil deeds.

Deadpool has always known there's more to his universe, and 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine proved that his fourth wall-breaking antics were actually prophetic — whether he realized it or not. What we didn't expect was for Wolverine to be part of the joke, turning a meta gag into an actual plot point that briefly tossed Wilson into the Earth-616 timeline. After multiversal merc-madness introduced some new characters and revived some classics, the pair of Canadian anti-heroes ended up in Earth-10005 with the other Fox movie X-Men, with many wondering how these two characters would ever fit into the MCU again.

Since then, both Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman have denied any involvement in the upcoming Doomsday film, but it seems they may have been lying to keep their trail cold. While their actual involvement remains under wraps and whether or not they actually appear in the film, but both actors are credited as contributors to writing of the story. Ultimately, that could mean anything, but both characters would offer a lot of insight into the multiverse if they showed up and joined the battle.

There are a handful of other heroes whose multiversal vocabulary is still untested but might be aware of what is happening. Sam Wilson got a tease and warning about different dimensions from an incarcerated Samuel Sterns at the end of C aptain America: Brave New World . Based on one of the new scenes from Endgame's encore, Steve Rogers may also now be in the know after having a run-in with Loki not long after he was sent back to the 1940's to reunite with his unrequited romance, Peggy Carter.

Similarly, Tony Stark knew about the multiverse through Doctor Strange, but that was limited to branching timelines and he was not wholly aware of other dimensions. How Iron Man's actor ended up playing Victor Von Doom is something we will have to wait a few more weeks to find out, but at least the MCU won't be caught completely by surprise when Doomsday finally arrives on Dec. 18, 2026.

articles.title: Chris Evans Wants To Set The Record Straight On MCU Fans Still Calling Him Cap

articles.content:
It's a very exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, as we're just a few weeks away from one of the most highly anticipated upcoming Marvel movies in years, Avengers: Doomsday . This is a big moment for fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order , as it'll be a massive crossover featuring a huge ensemble of heroes. That includes Chris Evans ' return as Steve Rogers, although he wants to set the record straight on fans still calling him "Cap." Let's break it all down.

Well, he certainly didn't mince words. We saw Anthony Mackie 's Sam Wilson became the new Cap during The Falcon and The Winter Soldier , eventually starring in Captain America: Brave New World. While Steve Rogers is returning for Doomsday , he's not going to be taking back that mantle. As we can see in the movie's footage, Steve is wearing street clothes and wielding Mjolnir, while Sam is still rocking the signature shield.

This latest trailer set the internet ablaze, thanks to both the new information about Steve's happy ending, as well as Cyclops saying the iconic line "To me, my X-Men." Fans are hyped about seeing entire teams of heroes unite agains Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom , namely The Avengers, The New Avengers, The Fantastic Four, and The X-Men. There's sure to be plenty of epic action throughout the movie's mysterious runtime, although fans are also expecting plenty of heartbreaking character deaths. After all, Infinity War and Endgame saw this happen to a number of beloved characters including Iron Man and Black Widow.

Undeterred by regional turbulence, Qatar is forging ahead with its plan to build a film and TV industry that intends to put the tiny Arab state rich in oil and gas on the global entertainment map.

That is the main takeaway of the recently concluded second edition of the Doha Industry Days, held Nov. 19-21 during the Doha Film Festival , attended by some 450 prominent executives from 38 countries. They included a robust contingent of Hollywood honchos, comprising Candle Media co-founder Kevin Mayer; Neon CEO and founder Tom Quinn; Mike Larocca, co-founder of Department M; Miramax boss Jon Glickman; Steven Paul, CEO of SP Media; and AGC Studios CEO Stuart Ford , to name a few. Talents on hand included "Squid Game" creator Hwang Dong-hyuk, "Avengers" director Joe Russo, Omar Sy and Noomi Rapace.

The Doha event took place despite regional instability caused by the U.S.-Iran-Israel war. In September Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival canceled its sixth edition that was scheduled to take place from Dec. 3 to 12 amid sharp escalation in its conflict with Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, who had targeted several Saudi cities.

"Obviously, you know the journey has not been easy," Al Thawadi said in his concluding remarks, alluding to the impact on Qatar of the ongoing regional conflict involving the U.S., Israel and Iran. The conflict has delayed plans to shoot a Doha-set contemporary adaptation of William Shakespeare’s “Othello” that Oyelowo will direct and star in alongside Rachel Brosnahan and Cynthia Erivo, being produced by Barbara Broccoli that was announced during the Doha Industry Days last year. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"But most of you are engaging with us; helping us build what we want to do," he added. "And what we've got here, it's a common vision, right? It's not my vision; it's not the Film Committee's vision. It is all our collective vision," Al Thawadi underlined.

Al Thawadi went on to vow that next year's edition of the Doha Industry Days "will be a lot bigger" and that, in the interim, there will more announcements, besides those that were made on the spot.

Those announcements included concrete plans for a Neon-backed biopic titled “Caesar" about Syrian military officer Farid Al-Madhhan who blew the whistle on torture and killings perpetrated by the regime of Syrian president Bashar Assad; and two other still untitled biopics, one on Egyptian music star Mohamed Mounir, known as El King; the other on controversial Lebanese pop star Fadel Shaker.

"The industry days here a year ago were something of a launch pad, where they laid out some broad parameters," Ford told Variety during a wide-ranging interview in Doha. "And we've seen in the last 12 months, Hassan Al Thawadi and his team have started to put building blocks in place," he said.

"They are also coming to the industry at a time of great change globally, which creates huge opportunity for them to earn a place at the table," the U.S. exec who has been long been active in the region went on to point out.
